purpose: Collect designated files from multiple VPS hosts into Cloudflare storage (R2 for file bodies, D1 for metadata) and let other devices download them by association.
requirements: Files at designated paths on multiple VPS hosts are collected into non-filesystem durable storage.
Other devices can discover and download those files.
Storage stack is Cloudflare Workers + D1 (metadata) + R2 (file bodies).
Synchronisation is scheduled, incremental, and content-hash deduplicated: only new or changed files are transferred.
Collection channel is Worker-direct SSH (decision D14): nothing is installed on the host; the Worker reaches it over cloudflare:sockets. This supersedes the earlier VPS-agent-push design (D3).
Hosts, their credentials, and the directories to collect from are runtime DATA added through the web UI, so adding a machine needs no redeploy; the only deployment secret is SSH_MASTER_KEY (D32).
No multi-statement atomicity may be assumed on D1; use object-level atomicity, idempotent writes, and compensating actions.
constraints: The SSH channel has no official Cloudflare support and cannot be verified locally (wrangler dev refuses outbound connections to private addresses), so the ssh-probe experiment must return a running answer before flow step 3 (D14, D27).
A Worker isolate has 128 MB of memory and no long-lived process, so large-file ingest must be chunked with the session state held in D1 (D8).

Authorization, current as of 2026-10-07: code writes, commits and PR pushes are allowed; deploying THIS Worker to the user's own Cloudflare account is allowed and was exercised (events e023, e024). Deploying anything to a VPS remains NOT authorized.

The deployed UI has NO authentication: anyone who can reach it can manage hosts and their stored credentials, and the /probe routes connect to a stored host. The user was shown this and accepted it on 2026-10-07 as a private-tool risk (D35). It must go behind Cloudflare Access or gain an API token before broader use.
web_fetch is unavailable on this machine, so platform limits must never be asserted from memory.
Node/pnpm/Python are not on PATH; use DSH-bundled runtimes.
acceptance: A file at a designated path on a remote host is collected and becomes retrievable by a second device.
Re-running collection with no file changes produces no new objects (idempotent, hash-deduplicated).
A changed file produces a new version while the previous version remains resolvable.
Metadata in D1 lets a consumer find a file by host and path without knowing the R2 object key.
Documented partial-failure and recovery behaviour for an interrupted collection.
